chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Jafar عليه السلام, who said:
The ʿAqilah is not liable for intentional acts, nor for confession, nor for settlement.

key_terms.إِقْرَارًا: a confession or admission establishing liability
key_terms.صُلْحًا: a legal settlement or negotiated agreement
key_terms.عَمْدًا: intentional action, as opposed to accidental harm
key_terms.ٱلْعَاقِلَةُ: the male paternal relatives who may collectively bear blood money in certain legal cases

ai.seo_question: When is the ʿaqilah not responsible for blood money in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the liability of the ʿaqilah, the paternal male kin who may bear blood money in specific cases. It clarifies that they do not bear liability in cases of intentional wrongdoing, liability established by confession, or liability fixed through settlement.
